samples.summary: `classLiteralOf` accepts the first string argument of ANY call expression, not just class-joining helpers, so it can point a future rewrite at a non-class literal
samples.evidence: Lines 221-229 only test `ts.isCallExpression(expr)` and then return the first direct string-literal argument, with no check of the callee identifier (`cn`/`clsx`/`classNames`/`twMerge`). `className={t("nav.home")}` returns the i18n key, `className={getVariantClass("primary")}` returns the variant name. The function's own doc (lines 193-195) states the whole point of the directness guard is to avoid "handing `inject.mjs` a confident pointer at a literal it would then REWRITE" — but the callee is never constrained, so exactly that pointer is produced for any single-string-argument call. Impact is a source rewrite of the wrong literal (silent corruption); it also pollutes `fpx` with a token that is not a class.

samples.summary: `findJsxRoots` registers no root for `forwardRef(...)`/`memo(...)`-wrapped components or anonymous default exports, making those whole components unaddressable
samples.evidence: The VariableStatement branch (lines 491-500) only accepts an initializer that is literally an ArrowFunction or FunctionExpression (`const fn = ts.isArrowFunction(init) || ts.isFunctionExpression(init) ? init : null`), so `const Button = forwardRef((props, ref) => <button/>)` and `const X = memo(() => <div/>)` produce no root under any name — the inner arrow is never registered either, because only the FunctionDeclaration/VariableStatement branches call `addRoot`. Likewise `export default () => <div/>` and `export default function () {}` (anonymous, `node.name` falsy at line 484) yield neither a root nor a `defaultExport`. `packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:69` already declares `kind: 'function' | 'forwardRef'` as a supported component kind, so forwardRef is in scope for this model. Consequence: `resolveNode` answers "no JSX-returning function named X" for a component that plainly exists, and a scene built from `roots` shows nothing for that file.
searchedFor: grep for forwardRef(/memo( in packages/frontend/src (no matches, but the module targets arbitrary consumer trees per its own header and tsconfig comment)
grep 'export default (' / 'export default memo' in packages/frontend/src

samples.evidence:
`pushExpr` only descends into function bodies passed as call ARGUMENTS (lines 368-370). An immediately-invoked function — `{(() => { return
; })()}` — has no function argument, so its JSX contributes no child; the callee is never inspected. Similarly `ts.isAsExpression`/`ts.isNonNullExpression` are not unwrapped (`{(
) as ReactNode}` disappears), and `const el =
; return
{el}
` numbers nothing for `el` because a variable initializer that is not a function is never a root. Each case is a rendered element the client outline cannot show and a write cannot target.

samples.summary: The `owner !== node` refusal message always blames a `{…}` expression, even when the owner is a ternary, `&&`, or parenthesised return with no braces involved
samples.evidence: Lines 739-746 emit "sits inside a {…} expression" whenever `hit.owner !== hit.node`. But `owner` is also the ConditionalExpression for `return cond ? <A/> : <B/>` (pushExpr line 356-359 forwards the returned expression as owner), and the ParenthesizedExpression for `return ((<div/>))` (rootJsxOf's `take` at line 445 unwraps only one paren level). In both cases the refusal names a construct that does not exist in the user's source, which is exactly the kind of wrong diagnosis the module's other comments call out as expensive.

samples.summary: `addRoot` still overwrites on a duplicate name, so `roots[name]` silently holds the LAST claimant while only `resolveNode` refuses it
samples.evidence: `if (name in roots) ambiguous.add(name); roots[name] = root;` (lines 478-479). `ambiguous` is consulted only inside `resolveNode` (line 682). Any other consumer named in the header — `extract.mjs` building `SceneMeta.roots`, or the `data-wb-node` stamper — reads `roots` directly and will render/stamp the second `Row`'s tree under the name while the first is invisible, i.e. the outline shows one function's nodes labelled as another's. Storing both (or omitting ambiguous names from `roots`) would make the refusal uniform.

samples.summary: `fp`/`fpx` are truncated to 32 bits, so an accidental hash collision can make the unique-match search resolve an anchor onto a different node
samples.evidence: `createHash('sha1')…slice(0, 8)` (lines 614 and 644) keeps 8 hex chars = 32 bits. `resolveNode` resolves on "exactly one match" of `fp`/`fpx`; a chance collision between two structurally different nodes in a large file (~2000 nodes gives roughly a 1-in-2000 chance of some collision per file by the birthday bound) either turns a genuinely unique node into a refusal, or — when the anchor's real node was removed — makes an unrelated node the sole match and the edit lands there silently, the failure the file is explicitly built to prevent. The `tag` guard only protects the path-hint branch, not the search branches.

samples.summary: `typescript` is imported at runtime by jsx-nodes.mjs but declared only as a devDependency
samples.evidence: `src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs:21` does `import ts from 'typescript'` and the tsconfig comment (lines 30-32) says these `.mjs` files are run directly by Node "inside the consumer's dev server". `package.json` lists `typescript` under `devDependencies` with no `dependencies`/`peerDependencies` entry, so once this package is installed into a consumer project (its stated purpose) the import fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. It only survives today because the package is `private: true` and resolves TypeScript from the workspace root.

samples.summary: `defaultExport` is recorded only when the default-exported function itself contains JSX, and `isExportAssignment` also matches TS `export = X`
samples.evidence: Line 486-489 nests the `defaultExport` assignment inside `if (root)`, so `export default function Page() { return renderPage(); }` leaves `defaultExport` null even though the default export is unambiguous. Separately, line 501 `ts.isExportAssignment(node)` matches `export = Foo` as well as `export default Foo` (they differ by `isExportEquals`), so a CommonJS-style `export = ` would be reported as the default export.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is genuinely present: classLiteralOf (jsx-nodes.mjs:224-229) only checks ts.isCallExpression(expr) and returns the first direct string/no-substitution-template argument, with no constraint on the callee identifier. So className={t("nav.home")} or className={getVariantClass("primary")} yields a literal that is not a class blob, exactly the pointer the function's own doc (lines 188-195) says it exists to avoid producing. I could not refute on 'not-present' (the code reads as described) nor on 'already-guarded' (no caller or callee filter exists anywhere; attrsOf at 164-167 calls it unconditionally for any className). Impact today is bounded: the only in-repo consumer is attrsOf -> fpxOf (line 574), a search key that is recomputed by the same function on both sides, so it cannot by itself resolve a wrong node (resolveNode requires a unique match, line 701); and inject.mjs, the rewriter named at line 195, does not exist in this package (only jsx-nodes.mjs, types.ts and tests are present), while every in-repo className call site uses cn(. That makes the 'silent source corruption' consequence latent rather than live, which is why confidence is low — but the helper is an exported, documented API explicitly aimed at 'arbitrary consumer trees' (lines 188-191), and its stated invariant about not handing a confident pointer at a non-class literal is not upheld, so I keep the finding rather than drop it on a judgement call.

verdict.reason: Verified in code: findJsxRoots' visit (jsx-nodes.mjs:482-505) only calls addRoot from the named-FunctionDeclaration branch (484-489) and the VariableStatement branch whose initializer must literally be an ArrowFunction/FunctionExpression (495-498). A CallExpression initializer such as forwardRef((props, ref) => <button/>) or memo(() => <div/>) is skipped by `if (!fn) continue`, and the inner arrow is never registered because no other code path calls addRoot. Anonymous default exports are also lost: line 484 requires node.name, and line 501 requires ts.isIdentifier(node.expression), so `export default function () {…}` and `export default () => <div/>` produce neither a root nor defaultExport. resolveNode (688-691) then answers "no JSX-returning function named X", making the component unaddressable and absent from any scene built from roots. I searched for a counterexample and found none: the package contains only jsx-nodes.mjs and types.ts, no other module in the repo implements this model (__wbReturns/returnsRoot/SceneMeta match only this file, types.ts and docs), there is no forwardRef/CallExpression unwrapping anywhere, and the docs (design-editor-engine.md:777-780) promise "one walkable root per JSX-returning function" with no stated carve-out. The shape is reachable on files that exist here: packages/frontend/src/components/color-swatch-button.tsx:29 and packages/frontend/src/components/ui/toolbar.tsx:86 are forwardRef-wrapped JSX-returning components that would register no root. Real logic gap with silent wrong-answer behavior for a core flow, in the correctness lane.
